title: Three study identifiers supply matched 12-month drought contrasts in a 2024 bird data release
abstract: We tested whether a public bird drought workbook permits repeated severity tests within the same study, species, response metric, location and control. The 2024 Dryad release has 319 rows and 204 species. Of 292 rows with 12-month drought magnitude, 51 rows in 17 matched groups from three study identifiers have within-group variation. Hawaii supplies 42 rows and 59 percent of the within-group exposure sum of squares. Two other studies are in southeast Australia. All matched drought records are from the 2000s, so the same test cannot be repeated in an independent period. Equal-row descriptive slopes are -0.901, +0.212 and +0.120 standardized effect units per severity unit. The pooled slope changes from +0.090 to -0.555 with inverse-variance weights. The source also repeats case identifiers across studies and labels one egg series as fledglings. These fixed-release descriptions do not establish a common severity response or its absence. Shared drought events, changing effect-size denominators, missing outcomes, detection and publication bias limit inference. The package gives an audit method, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions. It tests no air pollution effect.

display.caption: Only three study identifiers provide matched numerical drought-magnitude contrasts under the specified rule. Equal-row descriptive slopes have different signs. Circles use 12-month magnitude and crosses use 3-month magnitude. Connecting lines are not uncertainty intervals. The nest metrics label covers the source egg and fledgling label mismatch.
